report: ITERATION 3 convergence re-review of PR #1973 (issue #1745). The iteration-2 fix is CORRECT and COMPLETE: lib/test/lint-brand-devflow-sweep.py now fails closed on an unreadable tracked file. iter_blobs(root, skipped) catches OSError, breadcrumbs to stderr, and appends the path to a caller-supplied skipped list; scan threads it through; cmd_check allocates its own skipped list, emits a named finding per skipped path, and returns 1 — closing the AC3 forward-guard hole where a new renameable DevFlow in an unreadable file could escape classification. All three dispatched agents (code-reviewer, silent-failure-hunter, pr-test-analyzer) independently confirm nothing at or above Important. Non-gating modes (--update-baseline, --print-population) correctly pass no skipped list per the documented breadcrumb-and-continue contract, and cannot become a gate hole because any subsequent --check re-encounters the file and fails closed. The OSError catch fails toward RED (loud), the safe direction for a completeness lint. run.sh coverage exercises the fail-closed path via a portable dangling-symlink probe (docs/dangling.md -> rc=1 + named finding) layered on an established clean rc=0 tree, plus both reconciliation directions (forward unclassified/drifted, reverse stale-baseline/stale-provenance) with rc + named-finding assertions, and a real-tree green gate. Only Suggestion-level observations remain, all either already-parked advisories or peripheral coverage of bucket branches outside the fix delta. NO NEW at-or-above-Important finding introduced by the fix delta.
